subsystems.name: Electrode interface
subsystems.role: the tissue-facing array that records from and stimulates neurons at single-cell scale.
parts: penetrating microelectrode shanks or flexible threads

subsystems.name: Encapsulation and delivery
subsystems.role: keeps the body from attacking the device and the device from poisoning the body.

subsystems.name: Transceiver and power
subsystems.role: moves thousands of neural channels in and out through skin without wires.

subsystems.name: Compute core
subsystems.role: the 'expansion' itself — silicon that adds memory and parallel processing to the biological circuit.

subsystems.name: Coding and decoding stack
subsystems.role: software that turns spikes into usable signals and back into stimulation.

subsystems.name: Surgical and maintenance system
subsystems.role: places the array precisely and keeps it working for decades.

buildSteps.title: Design the array
buildSteps.detail: Choose how many electrodes, their spacing and stiffness so they reach neurons without tearing tissue.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate in a cleanroom
buildSteps.detail: Deposit and pattern metal and insulator layers on a flexible polymer or silicon wafer using the same lithography used for computer chips.

buildSteps.title: Encapsulate and test
buildSteps.detail: Coat every surface except the electrode sites, then soak-test for months to prove nothing leaks or corrodes.

buildSteps.title: Build the transceiver
buildSteps.detail: Design an application-specific chip that amplifies, digitises and multiplexes thousands of weak neural signals.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the compute module
buildSteps.detail: Pair the transceiver with a low-power accelerator and memory, keeping the total heat and power low enough for living tissue.

buildSteps.title: Implant
buildSteps.detail: A surgeon or robot inserts the electrodes into the target cortical area and seats the sealed electronics under the skull or behind the ear.

buildSteps.title: Record and train
buildSteps.detail: The system observes neural activity while the user performs tasks, and decoders learn which patterns correspond to which intentions.

buildSteps.title: Close the loop
buildSteps.detail: Add stimulation so the device can write information back, not just read it — the step that would make it an extension of memory rather than a sensor.

buildSteps.title: Maintain over decades
buildSteps.detail: Monitor signal quality, retrain decoders as the tissue shifts, and provide a safe way to remove or replace failed hardware.

prerequisites.why: clinical arrays today record from roughly a hundred electrodes and research devices reach a few thousand, but signals fade over months to years.
the brain forms scar tissue around implanted electrodes, which is the main reason recordings degrade.

prerequisites.tech: Wireless power and data through tissue
prerequisites.why: demonstrated in early human trials, but bandwidth and heat limits are far below what an added compute layer needs.

prerequisites.tech: Decoding of abstract content, not just movement
prerequisites.why: today's decoders reliably read intended movement; reading or writing memory and reasoning is not solved.
stimulation works coarsely but cannot yet address individual neurons without damaging them.

prerequisites.tech: Verification of device and data security
prerequisites.why: a networked implant that influences thought would need guarantees no such system currently provides.

pathway.milestone: clinical trials restore communication and cursor control for paralysed people using implanted arrays
pathway.unlocks: proof that the brain tolerates and can drive a digital interface.

pathway.milestone: arrays that stay functional for many years and thousands of channels, placed with robotic surgery
pathway.unlocks: richer signals and practical daily use, not lab sessions.

pathway.milestone: reliable two-way interfaces with fast wireless links
pathway.unlocks: the possibility of adding rather than replacing function.

pathway.milestone: a silicon layer that the cortex treats as part of itself, adding memory and parallel processing
pathway.unlocks: the stated goal — but it requires solving tissue integration, decoding of abstract thought and security together, none of which is close.
